document_metadata.document_type: Mainframe Batch To .NET 8 Target Design Specification

source_system_summary.processing_description: Ad-hoc dynamic SQL (PREPARE/EXECUTE) followed by a dynamic CALL of COBTUPDT in the same unit of work.

steps: STEP1 IKJEFT01: DSN RUN PROGRAM(CBTRNDYN) PLAN(CARDDEMO) PARMS('COBTUPDT')
outputs: Dynamic statement applied, then COBTUPDT's changes, committed together
RC 8 when EXECUTE fails (lost after COBTUPDT, GAP-007)

business_rules.statement: DYNSQL lines starting with '--' are skipped; columns 1-72 of the other lines are concatenated, each followed by one blank, into an 800-byte statement.
The statement is PREPAREd and EXECUTEd; the EXECUTE SQLCODE is displayed (statement errors surface at EXECUTE under ocesql).
A failed PREPARE or EXECUTE sets RETURN-CODE 8 and processing continues.
The program named in PARMS is CALLed dynamically (CALL identifier); COBTUPDT's STOP RUN ends the run unit, so 'CBTRNDYN: END' is not reached.

gaps.description: Plugin numeric convention prescribes MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero; the legacy source has no ROUNDED and golden fixtures prove truncation (i02-tie-half-cent). Legacy truncation is kept (ADR-003).

SQLCODEs come from Open COBOL ESQL over PostgreSQL, not Db2: unique violation -403, any other error -400, no row found 0 (+100 never raised). Under PostgreSQL a failed statement aborts the whole unit of work (d03: COBTUPDT's later UPDATE also fails); Db2 would roll back only the failed statement. The port reproduces the golden (PostgreSQL) behaviour; a savepoint-per-statement policy is a migration decision (ADR-007).
After CALL COBTUPDT the run unit ends at COBTUPDT's STOP RUN with COBTUPDT's RETURN-CODE, so CBTRNDYN's RC 8 from a failed EXECUTE is lost (d03 ends RC 4). Kept as observed (ADR-007).
